note: Yoga poses, guided sequences and programmes (D-026, D-027). Wording avoids medical claims; no breath retention anywhere. Images are AI-generated and captioned as such.

poses.name: Mountain Pose
poses.summary: The base of every standing pose. It looks like simply standing, and teaches steady alignment and attention.
poses.breathTip: Breathe slowly through the nose, feeling the breath rise from the feet to the crown on each inhale.
steps: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart, weight spread evenly across both feet.
Engage the thighs, gently lift the kneecaps and lengthen the tailbone toward the floor.
Roll the shoulders back and down, letting the arms rest beside the body, palms facing forward.
Lengthen the back of the neck and imagine a thread lifting the crown of the head toward the sky.
Soften the face, jaw and eyes while keeping the body alert and tall.
Hold and breathe steadily, grounding down through the feet with every exhale.
benefits: Practises even weight through both feet
Builds awareness of posture and alignment
A quiet way to arrive before the rest of a session
cautions: Those with low blood pressure should rise slowly out of the pose
If balance is difficult, stand near a wall for support

sources.name: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India

poses.name: Tree Pose
poses.summary: A one-legged balance where a steady gaze does most of the work, like a tree that sways but stays rooted.
poses.breathTip: Fix the gaze (drishti) on one still point and let each exhale root the standing foot deeper.
steps: Stand tall in Tadasana and shift your weight slowly onto the left foot.
Place the right sole against the inner left thigh or calf — never against the knee.
Bring the palms together in Anjali Mudra at the heart, elbows relaxed.
Fix your gaze on a fixed point ahead at eye level.
On an inhale, raise the joined palms overhead, keeping the shoulders soft.
Hold for several slow breaths, then release and repeat on the other side.
benefits: Strengthens the legs and ankles
Practises steady attention on a single point
Gently opens the hips and inner thighs
cautions: Avoid if you have acute ankle or knee injury
Those prone to dizziness should practise near a wall
Keep the neck relaxed if raising the arms causes strain

sources.name: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India

poses.name: Downward Facing Dog
poses.summary: A familiar full-body stretch with the hips lifted high, which also gives the arms and legs a change of load.
poses.breathTip: Let the breath be audible and oceanic (ujjayi); exhale as the heels reach toward the earth.
steps: Begin on all fours, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Tuck the toes, press into the palms and lift the hips high, forming an inverted V.
Keep a soft bend in the knees at first; lengthen the spine before straightening the legs.
Press the bases of the fingers down, rotate the upper arms outward and relax the neck.
Let the head hang heavy between the arms; gaze toward the navel.
Breathe for 5–10 rounds, pedalling the feet gently, then release to all fours.
benefits: Stretches the backs of the legs, shoulders and spine
Builds strength in the arms, shoulders and wrists
A refreshing pose to move through between others
cautions: Avoid with carpal tunnel syndrome or late pregnancy
Keep knees bent if hamstrings are very tight
Those with uncontrolled high blood pressure should keep the head above the heart

poses.name: Triangle Pose
poses.summary: A wide standing pose that lengthens one side of the body at a time while the chest stays open.
poses.breathTip: Inhale as you extend the top arm skyward; exhale and rotate the chest open a little more.
steps: Stand with feet 3–4 feet apart, right foot turned out 90 degrees, left foot slightly in.
Raise both arms to shoulder height, palms down, reaching actively.
Exhale and hinge sideways over the right leg, bringing the right hand to the shin, ankle or floor.
Extend the left arm toward the ceiling, stacking the shoulders in one line.
Turn the chest and gaze upward (or down toward the floor if the neck strains).
Stay for 5 breaths, press firmly into the feet and rise on an inhale. Repeat left side.
benefits: Stretches the sides of the body and the legs
Builds steadiness in the legs
Encourages easy breathing with an open chest
cautions: Avoid or modify with low blood pressure and neck problems
If hamstrings strain, bend the front knee slightly or use a block
Practise gently in case of diarrhoea or migraine

sources.name: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India

poses.name: Warrior I Pose
poses.summary: A lunge with the arms overhead, named for a warrior of Indian tradition. Strong legs, a lifted chest and a steady gaze.
poses.breathTip: Inhale tall through the crown, exhale and sink a little deeper into the front knee.
steps: From standing, step the left foot back 3.5–4 feet, turning it out about 45 degrees.
Bend the right knee directly over the ankle, thigh approaching parallel to the floor.
Square the hips forward as much as possible, drawing the right hip gently back.
Raise both arms overhead, palms facing or touching, shoulders melting away from the ears.
Lift through the chest and crown while grounding through the back heel.
Stay for 5 breaths, straighten on an exhale and repeat on the other side.
benefits: Strengthens the legs, shoulders and back
Opens the hips and chest
Builds stamina and focus
cautions: Use caution with recent knee, hip or shoulder injury
Those with high blood pressure may keep hands on hips instead of overhead
Shorten the stance if balance is difficult

poses.name: Warrior II Pose
poses.summary: A wide, grounded stance with the arms reaching in opposite directions and the gaze over the front hand.
poses.breathTip: Long, even breaths; let the exhale soften the shoulders while the arms stay strong.
steps: Step feet 4–4.5 feet apart, right foot out 90 degrees, left foot slightly in.
Bend the right knee over the ankle so the thigh nears parallel to the floor.
Extend the arms at shoulder height, palms down, reaching actively from fingertip to fingertip.
Keep the torso centred between the hips; shoulders stacked over pelvis.
Turn the gaze out over the right fingertips, jaw soft.
Stay for 5 breaths, straighten the leg on an inhale and repeat left.
benefits: Strengthens and stretches the legs
Builds endurance in the legs and shoulders
Practises patience while the effort stays steady
cautions: Avoid with chronic knee injury or recent hip surgery
Neck issues: keep the head centred instead of turning the gaze
Reduce the bend of the knee if the stance tires quickly

poses.name: Standing Forward Bend
poses.summary: A forward fold from the hips that lets the head and arms hang heavy.
poses.breathTip: With each exhale, let the torso hang a fraction heavier; each inhale, lengthen the spine.
steps: From Tadasana, inhale and sweep the arms up; exhale and hinge forward from the hips.
Keep the knees soft at first and fold over the fronts of the legs.
Let the head hang, holding the elbows or bringing fingertips to the floor or shins.
Draw the sitting bones toward the ceiling and release the crown toward the ground.
Soften the belly against the thighs with every exhale.
To rise, engage the core and roll up vertebra by vertebra on an inhale.
benefits: Stretches the backs of the legs and the back
A calm, inward-turning shape for a short rest
Lets the neck and shoulders soften
cautions: Rise very slowly to avoid dizziness; those with low blood pressure take care
Bend knees generously with back injury or hamstring tears
Avoid deep holds in late pregnancy

poses.name: Cobra Pose
poses.summary: A gentle backbend where the chest lifts and the legs stay grounded, like a cobra raising its hood.
poses.breathTip: Inhale as you rise, feeling the chest expand; exhale to lower down with control.
steps: Lie face down, legs extended, tops of the feet pressing into the mat.
Place hands under the shoulders, elbows close to the body, forehead resting down.
Press the pubic bone and legs firmly into the floor.
On an inhale, slowly lift the head, chest and upper abdomen — using back muscles more than arms.
Keep the elbows slightly bent and hugged in; shoulders away from the ears.
Hold a few breaths and exhale slowly back down. Repeat 2–4 times.
benefits: Strengthens the back muscles
Opens the chest and the front of the shoulders
Counters long hours of sitting with a light extension
cautions: Avoid in pregnancy and with herniated disc flare-ups
Those with carpal tunnel syndrome should keep weight off the wrists
Stop if the lower back pinches — reduce the height of the lift

sources.name: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India

poses.name: Child's Pose
poses.summary: A resting fold over the knees, often used between more active poses.
poses.breathTip: Breathe into the back of the ribcage — let each exhale sink the hips heavier toward the heels.
steps: Kneel with big toes touching and knees together or wide as comfortable.
Exhale and fold forward, laying the torso between or on the thighs.
Rest the forehead on the mat and let the shoulders release.
Arms can rest alongside the body, palms up, or extended forward, palms down.
Let the weight of the head fully surrender to the floor.
Stay for 10 or more slow breaths; to rise, walk the hands back and lift gently.
benefits: Gently stretches the back, hips and shoulders
A comfortable place to return to the breath
Suits a pause at any point in a session
cautions: Keep knees wider if pregnant or with knee injury
Those with ankle issues may place a rolled blanket under the shins
If the forehead cannot reach, rest it on stacked fists or a block

poses.name: Thunderbolt Pose
poses.summary: A kneeling seat on the heels, traditionally used for sitting quietly and for breath awareness.
poses.breathTip: Breathe deep into the belly; notice how the upright spine makes each breath naturally slow.
steps: Kneel with the knees together and the tops of the feet flat on the floor.
Sit back so the sitting bones rest on the heels, thighs touching.
Rest the hands palms-down on the thighs, shoulders relaxed.
Lengthen the spine tall, chin parallel to the floor, gaze soft ahead.
Breathe slowly for 1–5 minutes, keeping the belly soft.
If the ankles ache, place a folded blanket under the knees or shins.
benefits: Gives a steady, upright seat
Stretches the ankles, knees and thighs
A simple position for a few minutes of quiet
cautions: Place a cushion between heels and hips if knees are sensitive
Those with knee ligament injuries should avoid long holds
Numbness in the feet is a signal to come out and shake the legs

sources.name: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India

poses.name: Easy Pose
poses.summary: The easy cross-legged seat, a comfortable base for sitting and breath practice.
poses.breathTip: Sit tall and let the breath become silent and even — the measure of a well-seated posture.
steps: Sit on the front edge of a cushion so the knees drop below the hips.
Cross the shins, each foot resting beneath the opposite knee.
Place the hands on the knees, palms down or in Chin Mudra.
Rock side to side a few times and settle the sitting bones evenly.
Lift through the crown, soften the shoulders, close the eyes or lower the gaze.
Breathe naturally for several minutes; switch the cross of the legs halfway.
benefits: Lengthens the spine in sitting
Opens the hips gently
A steady seat for quiet attention
cautions: Elevate the hips with a cushion if knees float high or ache
Avoid forcing the knees down — flexibility comes with time
Those with sciatica may prefer sitting on a chair with spine tall

poses.name: Lotus Pose
poses.summary: The classic lotus seat of meditation. It asks for open hips, so most people begin with half-lotus or an easy seat.
poses.breathTip: Let the breath become subtle and long; a true lotus seat turns breath itself into meditation.
steps: Sit in Dandasana with legs extended and spine tall.
Bend the right knee and cradle the foot, drawing it toward the navel.
Place the right foot on the left hip crease, sole facing upward.
Then draw the left foot over and up onto the right hip crease.
Rest the hands on the knees in Chin or Jnana Mudra, spine rising effortlessly.
Hold comfortably; release the legs in reverse order and repeat with the other leg first.
benefits: A balanced, stable seat for long sitting
Opens the hips, knees and ankles over time
Traditionally associated with meditation
cautions: Never force — open the hips for months with half-lotus first
Avoid with knee or ankle injuries and sciatica
Come out slowly if the legs fall asleep

poses.name: Seated Forward Bend
poses.summary: A seated forward fold that stretches the whole back of the body.
poses.breathTip: Inhale to lengthen the spine forward; exhale to fold a little deeper from the hips, never the neck.
steps: Sit in Dandasana, legs extended together, hands beside the hips.
Press the sitting bones down and lift the crown to lengthen the spine.
Inhale and raise the arms; exhale and hinge forward from the hip creases.
Hold the shins, ankles or feet — wherever the body reaches without strain.
With each breath, lengthen the front body; with each exhale, soften into the fold.
Eventually rest the abdomen on the thighs; breathe calmly for 1–3 minutes.
benefits: Stretches the back, hamstrings and calves
Encourages a slow, inward-turning pace
A quiet pose near the end of a session
cautions: Avoid deep folding with a slipped disc or severe back pain
Bend the knees generously if hamstrings are tight
Practise gently during asthma flare-ups
In pregnancy, ask your health professional before practising this pose.

poses.name: Half Lord of the Fishes

image.alt: Illustration of Half Lord of the Fishes

poses.summary: A seated spinal twist named for the sage Matsyendranath, turning from the belly and lengthening the spine.
poses.breathTip: Inhale to grow tall through the spine; exhale to rotate a little deeper from the belly, not the neck.
steps: Sit in Dandasana, then bend the right knee and step the foot outside the left thigh.
Bend the left knee and tuck the left foot beside the right hip (or keep it extended).
Place the right hand behind you; wrap the left arm around the right knee.
Inhale and lengthen the spine; exhale and twist to the right from the navel.
Keep both sitting bones grounded; turn the chest, then the gaze last.
Stay for 5 breaths and unwind slowly. Repeat on the other side.
benefits: Increases spinal movement and rotation
Stretches the shoulders, chest and outer hips
Leaves the body feeling lighter after a long sit
cautions: Avoid during pregnancy and with herniated discs
Keep the twist gentle with recent abdominal surgery
Never force the neck past the comfortable range

poses.name: Bridge Pose
poses.summary: A lying backbend where the hips lift to form a bridge between the shoulders and feet.
poses.breathTip: Inhale as you lift the hips; exhale and stay, feeling the chest reach toward the chin.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet hip-width apart and close to the sitting bones.
Arms rest alongside the body, palms down.
Press the feet and arms down and on an inhale lift the hips toward the ceiling.
Keep the thighs parallel — do not let the knees splay outward.
Optionally clasp the hands under the back and press the shoulders down to open the chest.
Stay for 5–8 breaths, then release slowly, spine lowering vertebra by vertebra.
benefits: Strengthens the legs, hips and lower back
Opens the chest and front of the body
A gentle backbend to prepare for deeper ones
cautions: Avoid with recent neck injury or cervical spondylitis
Keep the head still — never turn it while lifted
Those with knee problems should keep the feet wider
In pregnancy, ask your health professional before practising this pose.

sources.name: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India

poses.name: Shoulder Stand
poses.summary: The shoulder stand, a classic inversion that puts the weight on the shoulders and upper arms. Learn it with an experienced teacher.
poses.breathTip: Breathe slowly and fully; the chest is compressed, so let the belly and ribs do the work.
steps: Lie on your back with 1–2 folded blankets under the shoulders, head off the edge.
Lift the legs together and swing them overhead, supporting the back with the hands.
Walk the hands down the back toward the shoulder blades, elbows shoulder-width.
Straighten the legs and torso into one vertical line, chest toward the chin.
Press the upper arms down; keep the neck still and relaxed — no turning.
Stay for 1–3 minutes, then lower with control and rest in Shavasana.
benefits: Builds strength in the shoulders and upper back
Offers a new view and a steady, unhurried pace
Traditionally called the queen of the poses
cautions: Avoid during menstruation, pregnancy, high blood pressure and glaucoma
Never turn the head in the pose; keep the neck weight-free
Practise near a wall when learning; exit slowly to avoid dizziness

poses.name: Corpse Pose
poses.summary: Complete rest lying on the back at the end of practice, letting the body and breath settle.
poses.breathTip: Let the breath breathe itself. Follow it only if the mind wanders; otherwise, simply rest.
steps: Lie flat on your back, legs a little apart, feet falling open naturally.
Arms rest beside the body, palms turning toward the sky.
Tuck the chin slightly so the back of the neck lengthens.
Scan the body from crown to toes, consciously releasing each part.
Let the breath become quiet and unforced; release all effort of mind.
Remain 5–10 minutes; to leave, deepen one breath, wiggle the fingers and roll gently to the right before rising.
benefits: Lets the body rest after effort
Practises releasing tension on purpose
A quiet close that gathers the practice
cautions: Those with a sore low back may rest a bolster beneath the knees
Cover yourself with a blanket if the body cools in deep rest
If sleep comes, shorten the practice and rest earlier at night

sources.name: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India

poses.name: Chair Pose
poses.summary: A standing squat with the arms overhead, as if sitting back into an invisible chair.
poses.breathTip: Inhale as you sink, exhale and settle deeper — steady, unclenched jaw, soft eyes.
steps: Stand with feet together or hip-width, arms sweeping overhead with the inhale, palms facing each other.
Exhale and bend both knees, sinking the hips as if lowering onto a chair behind you.
Keep the weight in the heels and the knees tracking over the toes, not past them.
Draw the lower ribs in, lengthen the tailbone down and lift through the crown.
Stay for 30–60 seconds, then inhale to straighten and exhale the arms down.
benefits: Strengthens the thighs, calves and ankles
Builds stamina in the legs and back
Warms the body quickly
cautions: Avoid deep bending with acute knee or hip injury — take a shallower seat
Keep the neck relaxed; lower the arms to shoulder height if the shoulders tire
Those with low blood pressure should rise slowly afterwards

poses.name: Extended Side Angle
poses.summary: A deep lunge with a long diagonal line from the back foot through the fingertips.
poses.breathTip: Let each inhale lengthen the underside of the body; each exhale, turn the chest a little toward the sky.
steps: From a wide stance, turn the right foot out and bend the right knee to a right angle.
Lower the right forearm (or fingertips) onto the thigh — never collapsing the chest inward.
Inhale the left arm overhead and beside the left ear, palm facing down.
Roll the ribs open, gazing up under the armpit; press the back-edge of the back foot firmly.
Stay for 30–60 seconds, then inhale to rise and repeat on the left.
benefits: Stretches the sides of the body, hips and groin
Strengthens the legs
Opens the chest after hours of sitting
cautions: Keep the bent knee from drifting past the toes to protect the joint
Rest the hand on a block if the forearm on the thigh collapses the chest
Neck strain — look down instead of up if the cervical spine complains

poses.name: Warrior III
poses.summary: A one-legged balance with the body and back leg level, like a plank in the air.
poses.breathTip: Small, even breaths. If the breath runs short, come out, rest, and return lighter.
steps: From Warrior I, shift weight into the front foot and lean the torso forward over it.
Lift the back leg as the chest descends, hinging at the hip until body and leg form one line.
Arms reach forward (or rest on the hips while learning); hips stay square to the floor.
Micro-bend the standing knee; press back actively through the lifted heel.
Gaze at one still point; stay for 15–30 seconds, then rise and switch sides.
benefits: Builds single-leg strength and ankle steadiness
Strengthens the back of the body
Practises concentration, since balance asks for attention
cautions: Practise near a wall; touch fingertips to it when balance wanders
Avoid with acute hamstring pulls — keep the lift shallow
Do not lock the standing knee; a soft knee is a safe knee
In pregnancy, ask your health professional before practising this pose.

poses.name: Eagle Pose
poses.summary: An eagle-like balance with the arms and legs wrapped around each other.
poses.breathTip: Breathe into the squeezed shoulder blades; feel them spread apart on every inhale.
steps: Bend both knees, sink slightly, and wrap the right thigh over the left.
Hook the right toes behind the left calf (or rest them on the floor as a prop).
Wrap the left elbow under the right; bring forearms and palms toward touching.
Sink the hips lower, lift the elbows to shoulder height, and lean the torso slightly forward.
Fix the gaze on one point; stay for 20–30 seconds, unwrap, and repeat on the other side.
benefits: Stretches the shoulders and upper back
Stretches the hips and thighs
Practises focus while the limbs are wrapped
cautions: Recent knee surgery — keep the wrap shallow or skip the leg hook
Keep the standing knee bent but never strained inward
If the forearms won't touch, hold opposite shoulders instead
In pregnancy, ask your health professional before practising this pose.

poses.name: Cat–Cow Flow
poses.summary: A flowing movement between a rounded and an arched spine on hands and knees, matched to the breath.
poses.breathTip: Inhale into the arch (cow), exhale into the round (cat). Let the breath lead, the spine obey.
steps: Come to all fours: wrists under shoulders, knees under hips, spine neutral.
Inhale — drop the belly, lift the chest and tailbone, eyes softly up (Cow).
Exhale — press the floor away, round the spine to the ceiling, chin toward chest (Cat).
Move slowly and continuously for 8–12 rounds, letting the movement ripple to the tail.
Return to neutral and rest in Child's Pose for a breath.
benefits: Moves the spine gently, one segment at a time
Warms the back before other poses
Links breath and movement
cautions: Pad the knees with a folded blanket if they complain
Wrist issues — make fists or lower to forearms
Keep the neck movement gentle if you have cervical concerns

poses.name: Camel Pose
poses.summary: A kneeling backbend that opens the whole front of the body. Come up slowly and keep the neck easy.
poses.breathTip: Slow breaths into the opening chest. If panic or tears arrive, come up slowly and kneel quietly.
steps: Kneel with knees hip-width, thighs vertical; hands rest on the lower back, fingers down.
Press hips forward, lift the sternum and begin to lean the shoulders back.
Reach one hand, then the other, to the heels (tuck toes for more height).
Push the hips forward so they stay over the knees; let the head release back only if the neck allows.
Stay for 20–30 seconds, then lead with the chest to rise; rest in Child's Pose.
benefits: Opens the chest, shoulders and front of the thighs
Builds back strength and flexibility
Best practised after a good warm-up
cautions: Keep the hips stacked over knees — never let them drift back behind the legs
Avoid with recent abdominal or back surgery, or unmanaged high/low blood pressure
Support the lower back with hands instead of reaching the heels if the back pinches
In pregnancy, ask your health professional before practising this pose.

sources.name: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India

poses.name: Bound Angle Pose
poses.summary: A seated pose with the soles of the feet together and the knees falling open, also called Cobbler's Pose.
poses.breathTip: Long, soft breaths into the lower belly and groins; let gravity do the persuading.
steps: Sit tall with the soles of the feet together, knees wide.
Hold the feet like a book — or ankles — drawing the heels comfortably near the pelvis.
Root the sitting bones, lengthen the crown, and let the knees sink without pushing.
To deepen, fold forward from the hips, chest leading, spine long.
Breathe 1–3 minutes; rise by pressing through the hips, not jerking the neck.
benefits: Opens the hips and inner thighs
A comfortable seat for quiet breathing
Can be done with cushions under the knees
cautions: Never bounce the knees downward — patience, not force, opens groins
Place blocks or bolsters under the knees for groin or knee sensitivity
With sciatica, sit on a folded blanket to tilt the pelvis forward

poses.name: Head-to-Knee Pose
poses.summary: A seated forward fold over one extended leg, with the other foot drawn in.
poses.breathTip: Exhale to lengthen over the straight leg; inhale to grow tall again. Never round with violence.
steps: Sit tall, extend the left leg long, and place the right sole against the inner left thigh.
Let the right knee fall open naturally (support it on a cushion if it floats high).
Inhale both arms up, exhale and hinge over the straight leg, holding shin, ankle or foot.
Keep the extended kneecap lifted and toes drawing back toward you.
Stay for 45–90 seconds, breathing into the back of the leg; switch sides.
benefits: Stretches the back, hamstrings and calves, one side at a time
Encourages a slow, inward-turning pace
A calm pose before sitting or rest
cautions: Bend the straight knee generously if the hamstrings protest
Asthma or back injury — keep the torso raised, hold a strap around the foot
Never pull the head down by force; the fold comes from the hips
In pregnancy, ask your health professional before practising this pose.

poses.name: Fish Pose
poses.summary: A gentle chest-opening pose lying on the back, often done after shoulder stand.
poses.breathTip: Breathe deep and slow into the lifted chest; the throat opening may feel unfamiliar at first.
steps: Lie on the back, legs together or in Padmasana (the classical form).
Slide the hands palms-down beneath the hips, elbows close in.
Press the forearms and lift the chest high, letting the head tip back to touch the crown on the floor.
Keep almost no weight on the head — the lift must live in the chest.
Stay for 15–30 seconds, then lift the head before lowering, and rest.
benefits: Opens the chest, throat and shoulders
Counters a rounded upper back from sitting
Stretches the front of the hips when the legs are extended
cautions: Avoid with neck injury, cervical spondylosis or migraine
Most weight belongs on the elbows, not the crown of the head
High or low blood pressure — keep the head lifted on a cushion instead
In pregnancy, ask your health professional before practising this pose.

poses.name: Legs Up the Wall

image.alt: Illustration of Legs Up the Wall

poses.summary: Legs resting up a wall, a supported, restful inversion also called Legs Up the Wall.
poses.breathTip: Natural, unhurried breathing — let the exhale grow a little longer with every minute.
steps: Sit sideways against a wall, then swing the legs up as you lower the torso to the floor.
Scoot the hips close to the wall (a folded blanket under the hips adds softness).
Let the legs rest straight up, arms open to the sides or on the belly.
Close the eyes; stay 5–15 minutes, letting the legs be utterly heavy.
To leave, bend the knees, roll to the side and rest a breath before rising.
benefits: A restful pose after a long day on your feet
Lets the legs and lower back relax
Easy to hold for several quiet minutes
cautions: Glaucoma or unmedicated hypertension — keep the hips low and legs lower
Menstruation traditionally calls for the hips to stay on the floor without elevation
Numbness or tingling: bend knees, feet on the wall instead
In pregnancy, ask your health professional before practising this pose.

poses.name: Wheel Pose
poses.summary: The full wheel, or Urdhva Dhanurasana, a deep backbend lifting the whole body off the floor. Advanced, so learn it with a teacher and build up to it.
poses.breathTip: Keep the breath flowing steadily in the pose. The chest is already at full stretch.
steps: Lie on the back, knees bent, heels drawn in close to the sitting bones.
Bend the elbows and place the palms flat beside the ears, fingers toward the shoulders.
Press into the feet and hands, and lift the hips first, then the chest, to crown of head (pause here if needed).
Straighten the arms fully and lift to the top of the head off the floor.
Stay for 10–20 seconds; tuck the chin and lower with control — crown, shoulders, hips — then hug the knees.
benefits: Stretches the whole front of the body
Builds strength in the arms, legs and spine
A bold pose that asks for a thorough warm-up
cautions: Warm up shoulders and spine thoroughly — never enter cold
Avoid with back injury, carpal tunnel, heart conditions or recent surgery
Beginner's edge: practise bridge pose and shoulder-opening drills first
Come down slowly; rushing the exit strains the neck
In pregnancy, ask your health professional before practising this pose.

poses.name: Crow Pose
poses.summary: An arm balance with the knees resting on the upper arms, like a crow perched on its hands.
poses.breathTip: Short, steady breaths with the belly drawn in; the core, not the breath, holds you up here.
steps: From a squat, place the palms flat shoulder-width, fingers spread wide.
Rise onto the toes, snuggle the knees onto the backs of the upper arms.
Lean forward, shifting weight into the hands — let one foot, then both, leave the floor.
Round the upper back, press the floor away, and draw the heels toward the hips.
Gaze slightly ahead of the fingertips; stay for 10–20 seconds and land softly back to the squat.
benefits: Builds strength in the wrists, arms and core
Practises balance and body awareness
Teaches calm when you feel nervous about falling
cautions: Wrist or shoulder injury — practise the lifted variation on a block instead
Place a cushion in front of the face while learning; the fear lessens with padding
Pregnancy and carpal tunnel syndrome should skip this pose

modules.title: Morning Surya Flow
modules.description: Awaken gently with a flowing sequence that warms the major muscle groups and sets a steady tone for the day.

steps.title: Wake-up breathing
steps.instruction: Sit cross-legged, spine tall. Take five long breaths and set a quiet intention (sankalpa) for the day.

steps.title: Mountain Pose
steps.instruction: Stand tall, feet grounded, crown lifting. Feel the whole body arrive in the posture.

steps.title: Upward stretch
steps.instruction: Inhale and sweep the arms overhead, interlacing the fingers. Press the palms up and lean gently right, then left, lengthening the side body.

steps.title: Standing Forward Bend
steps.instruction: Exhale and fold forward from the hips. Let the head hang heavy, knees soft. Rise halfway on the breath, then fold again.
steps.breath: Exhale to fold · Inhale to lengthen

steps.title: Warrior I — right
steps.instruction: Step the left foot back and bend the right knee. Raise the arms overhead and gaze forward with courage.

steps.title: Warrior II — right
steps.instruction: Open the hips and arms to the side, gazing over the front fingertips. Let the legs burn gently and the breath stay calm.

steps.title: Downward Facing Dog
steps.instruction: Step back and lift the hips into an inverted V. Pedal the feet, press the palms evenly and let the head hang.

steps.title: Cobra Pose
steps.instruction: Lower to the floor and rise into a gentle backbend, drawing the heart forward between the shoulders.

steps.title: Child's Pose rest
steps.instruction: Fold back onto the heels and rest the forehead down. Feel the warmth the flow has created.

steps.title: Final stillness
steps.instruction: Sit up, rub the palms warm and cup the eyes. Take three deep breaths together, then begin the day.

modules.title: Beginner Foundation
modules.description: The essential first poses in one guided session, with simple alignment cues and an easy pace.

steps.title: Centering in Easy Pose
steps.instruction: Sit comfortably on a cushion, hands on the knees. Watch the breath without changing it for a minute.

steps.title: Mountain Pose
steps.instruction: Stand and find full-body alignment: feet even, thighs engaged, crown tall. This is the seed of every standing pose.

steps.title: Tree Pose — both sides
steps.instruction: Root one foot and place the other sole to calf or thigh, palms at the heart. Gaze softly at one point. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Triangle Pose — both sides
steps.instruction: Step wide, reach and fold sideways over the front leg, stacking the shoulders. Feel the whole side body breathe. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Thunderbolt sitting
steps.instruction: Kneel and sit on the heels, spine tall, hands resting on the thighs. Notice how compact and steady the posture feels.

steps.title: Cobra Pose — 3 rounds
steps.instruction: Lie down and rise into a modest backbend three times, moving with the breath rather than forcing height.

steps.title: Bridge Pose
steps.instruction: Roll onto the back, bend the knees and lift the hips. Keep the thighs parallel and the jaw soft.

steps.title: Supine twist
steps.instruction: Hug the knees in and drop them gently to the right, arms wide, head to the left. Then switch sides.

steps.title: Corpse Pose
steps.instruction: Let the whole body rest. Release the feet, the hands, the jaw. Allow the practice to settle like sediment in still water.

modules.title: Slow and Settled
modules.description: A slow, floor-based sequence with long exhales and supported shapes for the end of a busy day.

steps.title: Long-exhale breathing
steps.instruction: Sit or lie comfortably. Breathe in for 4 counts and out for 8. Let the exhale be a sigh you don't have to hold back.

steps.title: Thunderbolt sitting
steps.instruction: Kneel and sit back on the heels with a cushion if needed. Rest the hands low and soften the shoulders away from the ears.

steps.title: Seated side stretch
steps.instruction: Still kneeling, place the right palm on the floor and reach the left arm over the head, curving gently right. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Child's Pose — supported
steps.instruction: Fold forward, knees wide, arms long or folded under the forehead. Let the back widen like a leaf with every breath.

steps.title: Seated Forward Bend
steps.instruction: Extend the legs and fold halfway — elbows on the floor, head heavy. Rest here; there is nothing to reach.

steps.title: Half Lord of the Fishes — both sides
steps.instruction: Twist gently, one side then the other, wringing out the day's accumulated tension with each exhale.

steps.title: Bridge Pose — gentle
steps.instruction: Lie back and lift the hips only halfway. Let the pose be a soft arc, not a performance.

steps.title: Legs up the wall
steps.instruction: Slide the legs up a wall or rest the calves on a chair seat. Arms wide, palms up. Let gravity do the resting.

steps.title: Corpse Pose with scan
steps.instruction: Lie flat. Move awareness slowly from crown to toes, releasing each region. End by resting in the silence after the last exhale.

modules.title: Flexibility Journey
modules.description: Lengthen the back, sides, hips and shoulders with patient, breath-led stretching.

steps.title: Warm-up circles
steps.instruction: Stand and circle the shoulders, wrists, hips and knees. Warm tissue stretches; cold tissue complains.

steps.title: Standing Forward Bend — 3 rounds
steps.instruction: Fold and rise three times: first round knees bent, second fingertips to shins, third wherever the body honestly reaches.

steps.title: Downward Facing Dog
steps.instruction: Pedal the heels slowly, bend one knee as the other straightens, alternating for the full hold.

steps.title: Triangle Pose — both sides
steps.instruction: Stay with each side, long and low, reaching through both fingertips as if pulled by two ropes. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Seated Forward Bend
steps.instruction: Fold over extended legs, holding feet or shins. Every exhale, lengthen the spine first, then soften.

steps.title: Half Lord of the Fishes — both sides
steps.instruction: Twist each side with the spine long. Imagine the breath rinsing the space between the vertebrae.

steps.title: Dragonfly side leans
steps.instruction: Sit with legs wide, walk the hands toward the centre, then lean over each leg in turn, breathing into the inner thigh.

steps.title: Supine hamstring stretch
steps.instruction: Lie back, loop a strap or towel around one foot and extend the leg toward the ceiling, knee soft. Switch legs halfway.
steps.breath: Exhale the leg a little closer

steps.title: Corpse Pose
steps.instruction: Rest flat and let the new length settle into the body's memory. Openness on the mat becomes openness in life.

modules.title: Bedtime Wind-Down
modules.description: A dim, slow, floor-based sequence to close the day, with gentle folds and a long rest.

steps.title: Unwind breathing
steps.instruction: Sit on the bed or mat. Breathe in through the nose for 4, out through the mouth for 8, three times, then breathe only through the nose.

steps.title: Thunderbolt sitting — slow
steps.instruction: Kneel back onto the heels, eyes closed. Let the day's events pass like clouds; follow none of them.

steps.title: Neck & shoulder release
steps.instruction: Drop the right ear to the right shoulder and breathe; then left; then roll the shoulders slowly backward.

steps.title: Child's Pose — long hold
steps.instruction: Fold forward with knees wide and forehead down. Feel the breath move the lower back like a tide.

steps.title: Gentle Seated Forward Bend
steps.instruction: Extend the legs and rest forward over a cushion or bolster. Support the head so the neck does nothing.

steps.title: Supine twist — both sides
steps.instruction: Lie back and let the knees fall gently side to side, head opposite. Unwind the spine like a ribbon.

steps.title: Corpse Pose — yoga nidra light
steps.instruction: Lie flat, blanket over the body. Move awareness crown to toes once, then let the awareness itself dissolve. If sleep comes — accept it.

modules.title: Core Fire Vinyasa
modules.description: A strong flow that builds from the belly outward: sun salutations, boat, warriors, crow attempts and wheel. Come warmed up.

steps.title: Seated centering
steps.instruction: Sit tall in an easy seat. Take several easy breaths, set an intention for a steady practice, then three slow breaths to settle.

steps.title: Sun salutations ×4
steps.instruction: Full vinyasa rounds with low, slow chaturangas. Let each round be a little more precise than the last.

steps.title: Boat circuit ×2
steps.instruction: Navasana to half-lower and back, twice through. Legs and spine long; the low back stays honest.

steps.title: Warrior circuit — right
steps.instruction: Warrior I to II to side angle, 5 breaths each, hips sinking low and breath staying wide.

steps.title: Warrior circuit — left
steps.instruction: The mirrored circuit. Anchor the back heel; light up the standing leg.

steps.title: Crow Pose — attempts
steps.instruction: Three crow attempts with rests between: 3, 5 and 8 breaths. Cushion before the face; courage in the belly.

steps.title: Wheel Pose ×2
steps.instruction: Two full lifts, 5 breaths each, knees hugging between. Bridge is always an honourable variation.

steps.title: Twist & fold counter
steps.instruction: Seated twist each side, then a long forward fold to pour cool water on the fire.

steps.title: Shavasana
steps.instruction: Four minutes of complete stillness — the fire settles into warmth.

modules.title: Inversion Path
modules.description: A measured walk toward inversions, from legs up the wall to shoulder stand, with wall-supported options at each step.

steps.title: Settle & breathe
steps.instruction: Lie back with knees bent. Twelve slow breaths, exhale longer than inhale, preparing the neck and mind.

steps.title: Bridge — preparation
steps.instruction: Two bridges, lifting hips and chest, shoulders tucking under. Wake the upper back that will hold you.

steps.title: Legs Up the Wall
steps.instruction: Three minutes with legs rising — the gentlest inversion and the best teacher of letting go.

steps.title: Shoulder Stand
steps.instruction: From bridge, support the back with the hands, elbows shoulder-width. Legs rise quiet and vertical. Never turn the head.

steps.title: Plough Pose
steps.instruction: Lower the toes to the floor behind, hips stacked over shoulders. Stay for 8 breaths, arms pressing down.

steps.title: Fish Pose — counter
steps.instruction: Release the throat and chest after the inversion. Crown light, weight in elbows.

steps.title: Twist counter
steps.instruction: Supine twist each side, knees falling heavy, shoulders staying home.

steps.title: Shavasana
steps.instruction: Five minutes of integration. The body has seen its own reflection in stillness — let it look a while longer.

modules.title: Deep Opening Evening
modules.description: A long, quiet evening sequence for hips and hamstrings. Long stays, props welcome, no force.

steps.title: Long exhale settle
steps.instruction: Any comfortable seat. In 4 · Out 8 for ten rounds — the nervous system shifts gear before the body does.

steps.title: Half lotus preparation — both
steps.instruction: Ankle cradles and figure-four circles. The knee is sacred — no force, ever, in either direction.

steps.title: Full pigeon — right
steps.instruction: Shin forward, hips square, forehead toward the bolster. Three minutes of breathing into the deep glute.

steps.title: Full pigeon — left
steps.instruction: The other hip's own story. Same care, same patience.

steps.title: Deep seated twist — both
steps.instruction: Half Lord of the Fishes at full depth, spine lengthening on every inhale, twisting on every exhale.

steps.title: Wide-legged dragonfly
steps.instruction: Legs wide, walk the hands forward, chest lowering. Centre, then each side — long, silent holds.

steps.title: Seated Forward Bend
steps.instruction: The week's folds gather here. Hold the feet, forehead toward the shins, back body wide with breath.

steps.title: Legs Up the Wall
steps.instruction: Reverse the day. Four minutes of light, heavy legs.

steps.title: Shavasana
steps.instruction: Five minutes of complete release. The deepest flexibility is surrender.

modules.title: Restful Reset
modules.description: A short, restful session for a lighter day: a fold, legs up the wall and a long rest.

steps.title: Settle in
steps.instruction: Sit comfortably and let the breath settle. Notice where the body is holding on.

steps.title: Child's Pose
steps.instruction: Fold forward with the knees wide and the forehead resting down. Let the back widen with each breath.

steps.title: Legs up the wall
steps.instruction: Rest the legs up a wall or on a chair seat, arms wide, palms up.

steps.title: Corpse Pose
steps.instruction: Lie flat and release the feet, the hands and the jaw.
steps.breath: Let the breath move by itself

modules.title: Standing Strength
modules.description: A steady standing sequence of chair, warrior, side angle and balance poses, both sides each.

steps.title: Centering
steps.instruction: Sit tall in an easy seat and take several slow breaths.

steps.title: Mountain Pose
steps.instruction: Stand tall and feel the weight even through both feet.

steps.title: Chair Pose
steps.instruction: Bend the knees and sit back, arms overhead, chest lifted.

steps.title: Warrior I, both sides
steps.instruction: Step back into a lunge with the arms overhead. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Warrior II, both sides
steps.instruction: Open the hips and arms, gazing over the front hand. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Extended Side Angle, both sides
steps.instruction: Rest the forearm on the thigh and reach the top arm over the ear. Switch sides halfway.
steps.breath: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to turn the chest

steps.title: Warrior III, both sides
steps.instruction: Hinge forward and lift the back leg, keeping the standing knee soft. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Eagle Pose, both sides
steps.instruction: Wrap the arms and legs and sink into a small squat. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Standing Forward Bend
steps.instruction: Fold forward from the hips and let the head hang.

steps.title: Corpse Pose
steps.instruction: Lie flat and let the effort drain away.

modules.title: Hips and Twists
modules.description: An evening session of seated folds, hip openers and twists, ending with legs up the wall.

steps.title: Bound Angle Pose
steps.instruction: Sit with the soles of the feet together and the knees falling open. Sit on a folded blanket if the hips are tight.

steps.title: Cat-Cow Flow
steps.instruction: On hands and knees, arch and round the spine slowly with the breath.
steps.breath: Inhale to arch, exhale to round

steps.title: Head-to-Knee Pose, both sides
steps.instruction: Fold over one extended leg at a time. Switch sides halfway.
steps.breath: Exhale to lengthen over the leg

steps.title: Half Lord of the Fishes, both sides
steps.instruction: Sit tall and twist gently from the belly. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Seated Forward Bend
steps.instruction: Fold over both legs, bending the knees as much as you need.

steps.title: Bridge Pose
steps.instruction: Lift the hips with the feet hip-width apart.

steps.title: Legs up the wall
steps.instruction: Rest the legs up the wall and let the arms fall wide.

steps.title: Corpse Pose
steps.instruction: Lie flat and let everything rest.

modules.title: Balance and Focus
modules.description: A morning session of one-legged balances and a steady gaze, with a long rest to finish.

steps.title: Centering
steps.instruction: Sit tall and take slow, even breaths.

steps.title: Mountain Pose
steps.instruction: Stand tall with the weight even through both feet.

steps.title: Tree Pose, both sides
steps.instruction: Root one foot and rest the other sole on the calf or thigh. Gaze at one point. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Eagle Pose, both sides
steps.instruction: Wrap the arms and legs and settle into a small squat. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Warrior III, both sides
steps.instruction: Hinge forward and lift the back leg, keeping the standing knee soft. Switch sides halfway.

steps.title: Chair Pose
steps.instruction: Sit back into the invisible chair, arms overhead.

steps.title: Standing Forward Bend
steps.instruction: Fold forward and let the head hang.

steps.title: Child's Pose
steps.instruction: Fold forward on the knees and rest the forehead down.

steps.title: Corpse Pose
steps.instruction: Lie flat and release the body.
steps.breath: Let the breath move by itself

programs.title: First Steps
programs.description: Seven days of short sessions that introduce the basic poses and end with rest. About 10 to 15 minutes a day.

programs.title: Steady Practice
programs.description: Fourteen days that build standing strength, balance and hip movement, with a rest day each week.

programs.title: Deep Practice
programs.description: Twenty-one days for people with a regular practice: strong flows, inversions and long evening openers, with rest days. Ideally with an experienced teacher.
